title: Foreigners Buying Housing in Vietnam 2026: Conditions and Limits
desc: Can foreigners buy housing in Vietnam? Only within projects, up to 30% of apartments per building, 250 houses per area, 50-year ownership, one extension.
summary: Conditions, forms, quantities and ownership terms for housing owned by foreign individuals and organisations in Vietnam under the Housing Law 2023 and Decree 95/2024/ND-CP.
body: p

Many homeowners have relatives or partners who are foreigners wanting to buy housing in Vietnam. The law allows it but with many limits. This article summarises the Housing Law 2023 (effective 1 August 2024) and Decree 95/2024/ND-CP.
h2
1. Who may buy?
p
Under Clause 1, Article 17 and Article 18 of the Housing Law:
ul
Foreign individuals permitted to enter Vietnam who are not entitled to diplomatic or consular privileges and immunities.

Foreign organisations operating in Vietnam (foreign-invested enterprises, branches, representative offices, investment funds, foreign bank branches) holding a valid investment certificate or operating licence at the time of the transaction.
p

Documents for individuals: a valid passport with an entry stamp (or an equivalent legal document) and a written undertaking that they are not entitled to diplomatic privileges and immunities (Article 3 of Decree 95/2024/ND-CP).
h2
2. Where and how may they buy?
ul

Ownership is allowed only of housing within housing construction investment projects, including apartments and detached houses, and only where the project is not in an area requiring national defence or security (Article 16). The list of projects that may be sold to foreigners is announced by the provincial People's Committee.

Forms: buying or lease-purchasing commercial housing from the investor; receiving commercial housing in a project by gift or inheritance; or buying from a foreigner who already lawfully owns it (Clause 2, Article 17).
This means they may not buy individual houses or land in residential areas outside projects.
h2
3. Quantity limits
p
Under Article 19 of the Housing Law and Article 5 of Decree 95/2024/ND-CP:
ul
At most 30% of the apartments intended for residence in an apartment building; for a building with several blocks or houses sharing a podium, 30% is calculated for each block or house.
Detached houses: at most 250 houses in an area with a population equivalent to one ward, that is 10,000 people according to the plan.

A transaction exceeding the quantity or in a project that is not permitted has no legal validity, no Certificate is issued, and the seller must pay compensation (Clause 3, Article 7). The seller must therefore check information on the website of the provincial housing management authority before signing.
h2
4. Ownership term: 50 years, one extension
p

A foreign individual owns housing by agreement but for no more than 50 years from the date the Certificate is issued, and may extend once for no more than 50 years; the term is stated on the Certificate (Point c, Clause 2, Article 20). A foreign organisation owns for no longer than the term stated in its investment certificate.
p

To extend, the owner submits a dossier to the provincial People's Committee where the house is located at least 3 months before expiry; the provincial People's Committee responds within 30 days at most (Article 6 of Decree 95/2024/ND-CP). Before expiry the owner may sell or gift the house to a person entitled to own housing in Vietnam; if it is not sold or gifted by expiry, the house becomes public property.
p
A foreign individual who is married to a Vietnamese citizen living in Vietnam may own housing and has the same rights as a Vietnamese citizen.
h2
5. Obligations in use and leasing
ul
Payment for purchase or lease-purchase must be made through a credit institution or a foreign bank branch operating in Vietnam (Point c, Clause 2, Article 21).

An individual may lease the house for purposes the law does not prohibit, but must give written notice before leasing and within 15 days after the lease ends (Article 3 of Circular 05/2024/TT-BXD), and must pay tax on rental income.
A foreign organisation may use the house only to accommodate people working for that organisation.
A person who receives housing by gift or inheritance but is ineligible or beyond the quantity limit may only receive the value and is not issued a Certificate (Article 22).
p
A housing sale contract must be notarised or certified, except where buying from an investor that is an organisation – see Notarising Property Sale Contracts 2026.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The Housing Law 2023 and Decree 95/2024/ND-CP are currently partially no longer in effect; the Law and Circular 05/2024/TT-BXD still refer to "district-level housing management authority" under the former government model. When transacting, ask the Department of Construction where the project is located about where to send notices and the list of projects permitted for sale.
